You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.

questions.questionText: The table shows the estimated costs for operating a new factory at the end of its first year. costs $m building the factory 20 raw materials including fuel 5 machinery and delivery vehicles 4 wages for workers 1 Assuming the short run is one year, what are the total variable costs?

options.A: $1m B $6m C $10m D $30m

questions.questionText: A manufacturing company merged with two companies. One of these was company X that produced a substitute product. The other was company Y that supplied its raw materials. Which combination shows the types of merger that the manufacturing company has undertaken? merger with merger with company X company Y

options.A: horizontal horizontal
options.C: vertical horizontal

questions.questionText: Which phrase best describes the market structure illustrated by the diagram if the firm produces at output Q ? $ AC MC MR AR O Q quantity

options.A: a monopolistic firm in short-run equilibrium
options.C: an oligopoly engaged in a price war

questions.questionText: The government wants to regulate the consumption of a demerit good in order to increase society’s net welfare. In which situation will society’s net welfare increase?

options.A: The fall in the marginal social benefit is greater than the fall in the marginal social cost.
options.B: The fall in the marginal external cost is greater than the fall in the marginal external benefit.
options.C: The fall in the total social benefit is greater than the fall in the total social cost.
options.D: The fall in the total social cost is greater than the fall in the total social benefit.

questions.questionText: Governments often aim to reduce income inequalities. The diagram shows the effects of using taxation and benefits to try to achieve this aim. 100 000 average income per 80 000 household key ($ per year) original income 60 000 disposable income final income 40 000
000 bottom 2nd 3rd 4th top 20% 20% 20% 20% 20% household income What can be concluded from the diagram about the effects of taxes and benefits?

options.A: All income groups are better off except those originally earning more than $40000 per year.
options.B: Benefits paid to the lower income groups are not a burden because they are not paid out of tax revenues.
options.C: The average final income of the top 20% exceeds the combined final incomes of the other groups.
options.D: The progressive taxation system still favours the top 20% over the bottom 20% of households.

questions.questionText: Which policy is likely to be the least effective means of producing a more equal distribution of income amongst households?

options.A: the imposition of minimum wage levels below the levels produced by the market
options.B: the introduction of progressive personal income taxes
options.C: the payment of benefits to low income households
options.D: the removal of sales taxes on food consumed by lower income households

questions.questionText: Which supply curve (S) indicates that eventually an individual will choose to spend more time on leisure rather than continue working for increased wages?

options.A: B S wage wage S O O hours worked hours worked
options.C: D S S wage wage O O hours worked hours worked

questions.questionText: When is a trade union less likely to gain a large pay rise for its workers?

options.A: It represents a large proportion of the workforce in the company.
options.B: It represents a workforce that has an elastic demand for its labour.
options.C: It represents a workforce that is increasing its labour productivity.
options.D: It represents a workforce that works for a highly profitable monopoly firm.

questions.questionText: Which statement does not support the view that extraction of mineral resources by a foreign company will make it more difficult for a developing economy to achieve future economic growth?

options.A: Exports of these mineral resources will result in an appreciation of the exchange rate.
options.B: Reduced tax rates aimed at encouraging the foreign company to invest in the country will increase inflation.
options.C: The foreign company will raise the skill levels of the local population through training schemes.
options.D: The foreign company will send profits back to its own country.

questions.questionText: Growth rates can be calculated using changes in the value of GDP from year to year. Why is real GDP considered to be a better indicator than nominal GDP for this calculation?

options.A: Real GDP adjusts for price changes by using a base year.
options.B: Real GDP ignores the effects of fluctuations in exchange rates on purchasing power.
options.C: Real GDP includes changes in the size of the population.
options.D: Real GDP measures GDP at factor cost rather than market prices.

questions.questionText: What is a cause of seasonal unemployment?

options.A: a general decrease in the demand for goods and services
options.B: a lack of necessary skills in the workforce
options.C: a temporary change in the pattern of consumers’ expenditure
options.D: an unwillingness of workers to move to other parts of the country where there is work

questions.questionText: A firm initially employs 50 workers, each working 40 hours a week, and produces a total output of 18000 units. It then employs an additional 10 workers, again each working 40 hours, and total output rises to 19200 units. Which effect does this rise in employment have on labour productivity per hour?

options.A: decreases it by 1 unit
options.C: increases it by 120 units

questions.questionText: According to Keynesian theory, when will an increase in the money supply leave the level of output unchanged?

options.A: when there is a liquidity trap
options.B: when the money supply increase was not anticipated
options.C: when there is a floating exchange rate
options.D: when there is an immediate adjustment to expectations about future price levels

questions.questionText: An economy is experiencing a negative output gap. What is most likely to happen to the inflation rate and unemployment in this economy? inflation rate unemployment

options.A: decreases decreases
options.C: increases decreases

questions.questionText: What do Monetarists believe?

options.A: Economies are naturally unstable.
options.B: Policy makers should follow set rules targeting the money supply.
options.C: The aggregate supply curve has a slight slope.

questions.questionText: Which combination of changes over time in an economy would definitely represent increased economic growth per capita? average total Gini total output price level population coefficient

options.A: falls rises falls rises
options.C: rises falls falls rises

questions.questionText: Under which circumstances will the future burden of the national debt on a country increase the most? increase in the price of change in GDP budget deficit government bonds

options.A: +2% of GDP +4% decreasing
options.C: +4% of GDP +2% decreasing

questions.questionText: Country X has a low rate of inflation and a stable currency and unemployed resources. It attracts $25 billion of direct foreign investment. What is most likely to be a positive benefit of the inflow of this foreign direct investment for country X?

options.A: Aggregate demand will be boosted through the investment multiplier.
options.B: Country X will have to use its foreign reserves to eliminate any trade deficit.
options.C: The balance of payments will be affected with the outflow of profits to foreigners.
options.D: The rate of inflation will increase if country X tries to increase capacity.

questions.questionText: A country with an income tax rate X decides to increase its tax rate. The diagram shows tax revenue will fall. tax revenue O X tax rate Why would this happen?

options.A: Fewer goods will be produced.
options.B: People will work fewer hours to maintain incomes.
options.C: Prices will rise.
options.D: There will be an increase in tax avoidance.

options.A: inflation rate unemployment level
options.C: price level unemployment level
